title: Redacted
desc: Cover-ups, accidents that shaped nations & the strangest true stories

questions.q: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919 killed 21 people in Boston. How fast did the wave of molasses travel?
questions.a: About 56 km/h (35 mph) — a 7.5-metre wall of treacle

questions.q: Which US president served only 32 days before dying?
questions.a: William Henry Harrison — he caught pneumonia after giving the longest inauguration speech in history, in the rain

questions.q: The Dancing Plague of 1518 saw hundreds of people in Strasbourg do what for days?
questions.a: Dance uncontrollably — some reportedly died from exhaustion, strokes, or heart attacks

questions.q: What everyday object did a Scottish engineer invent after watching a ball roll across a muddy field?
questions.a: Trick question setup — but John Boyd Dunlop invented the pneumatic tyre after watching his son struggle to ride a tricycle on cobblestones

questions.q: The 'Night Witches' were an all-female squadron of bomber pilots in WWII. Which country were they from?
questions.a: The Soviet Union — the 588th Night Bomber Regiment, feared by the Germans

questions.q: What did Cleopatra's native language turn out to be — and it wasn't Egyptian?
questions.a: Greek — the Ptolemaic dynasty was Macedonian Greek. She was reportedly the first Ptolemy to learn Egyptian

questions.q: The Tunguska event of 1908 flattened 80 million trees in Siberia. What caused it?
questions.a: An airburst from a meteoroid or comet fragment — it exploded before impact with a force 1,000 times greater than the Hiroshima bomb

questions.q: How did Rasputin reportedly survive his assassination — at least initially?
questions.a: He was poisoned with cyanide-laced cakes and wine, shot multiple times, beaten, and finally drowned in the Neva River

questions.q: The Stonewall Riots of 1969 are considered the catalyst for which civil rights movement?
Which country accidentally invaded another country in 2007 — and apologised?
questions.a: Switzerland — soldiers accidentally marched into Liechtenstein during a training exercise at night
